analysis.investment_thesis: Optiemus scores poorly on both Magic Formula legs — Earnings Yield is a meager ~2.9% (EBIT INR 108 Cr / EV ~INR 3,724 Cr) and ROIC is roughly 14%, both well below my required thresholds of 15%+ and 20%+ respectively. The stock commands a premium (P/E 55.6x, EV/EBITDA 33x) that is completely unjustified for a thin-margin distributor with a troubled operating history.
key_strengths: Revenue recovery 2022→2025: INR 472 Cr → INR 1,890 Cr, approaching 2016 highs
Low financial leverage (D/E 0.32) after aggressively deleveraging borrowings from INR 239 Cr (2020) to INR 43 Cr (2022)
High promoter holding (72.17%) signals ownership alignment
key_risks: Earnings Yield ~2.9% — stock is deeply overvalued relative to operating earnings
FCF has been negative three of the last four years (FY23: -99 Cr, FY24: -21 Cr, FY25: -96 Cr) with capex consuming more than operating cash flow
Operating margins razor-thin at 5.28%; ROIC ~14% — insufficient for Magic Formula inclusion
red_flags: Revenue collapsed 90% from INR 1,922 Cr (2016) to INR 182 Cr (2021) — structural fragility, not a temporary dip
FY2021 net profit of INR 95 Cr was entirely artificial: Other Income alone was INR 206 Cr vs. operating loss of INR -98 Cr
Finance costs surged 4x to INR 30 Cr in FY25 — debt creeping back up to INR 247 Cr in borrowings
CWIP jumped from INR 3 Cr to INR 99 Cr in FY25 — large unproductive capex commitment building
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the Magic Formula, Optiemus fails on both dimensions. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) is approximately 2.9% — INR 108 Cr EBIT against an enterprise value of ~INR 3,724 Cr — barely a third of my 12% minimum threshold. Return on Capital is ~14% (consistent with the reported ROCE of 14.4%), below my 20% floor for a "good" business. A company must score high on BOTH metrics to merit attention; Optiemus is poor on both, making it a clear pass under the formula.

The business quality concerns are equally damning. The company's revenue literally imploded from INR 1,922 Cr in FY16 to INR 182 Cr in FY21 — a ~90% destruction of the top line in five years — before clawing back. That kind of history suggests the company lacks a durable competitive moat. Current recovery is real but the operating margins (5.28%) reflect classic commodity distribution economics, not the high-ROIC, capital-light franchises I seek. The market is pricing this at 55.6x earnings and 33x EBITDA — a valuation that would only be justified if the company were a compounding machine at 25%+ ROIC, which it demonstrably is not.
